note: The FFW_PLATFORM:* lines `franken-speaker --platform-startup --entropy-provider <legacy>` prints, as pinned examples (P02 / ffw-jub, root decision 5126). The default provider prints no `provider=` token, so every line in p02_platform_markers.json (which DarkPeak's smoke judge reads) is unchanged and this file is NOT part of it: the legacy provider is explicit, and its lines are judged here and by tests/p02/test_legacy_entropy.py. `provider=` appears on the ENTROPY line only, between `provenance=` and `reason=`, with one of the two values below, on PASS, REFUSED and NOT_RUN alike, so a transcript always shows which provider produced or refused its entropy. `legacy_dev_random_test_environment` means a caller named an admitted TEST ENVIRONMENT: a PASS is not an observation about any kernel and is not device evidence. `legacy_dev_random` (no test environment) is qualified by the committed guest evidence, which has no observation of the legacy device, so it is refused `unavailable` without a kernel call. Scenarios use test doubles: they prove the logic and the grammar, not the real backend and not any kernel. The reason codes are the closed set of p02_platform_markers.json; no code was added.
